consensus_summary: Consensus primary meaning is moral/spiritual evil, sin, spiritual blindness/ignorance, and separation from God (antithesis of divine light/salvation), with common alternatives of judgment, death, primordial chaos, and minority divine mystery or suffering/secrecy.
book_summary: Darkness means concealed disobedience—deeds hidden from the light.
book_core_identification: concealed disobedience (deeds hidden from the light)
boundary_disagreement: Book limits the primary referent to the concealment of evil deeds (per John 3:19-20), whereas consensus primary admits broader cases of sin, blindness, Satan’s domain, and separation even without explicit concealment; secrecy is only a rare/neutral alternative in consensus.
rationale: Minimum cores share the moral-evil referent drawn from the same Johannine texts, but the book materially narrows extension and precision to the hidden/disobedient aspect alone rather than the full dualistic complex of evil, ignorance, and separation; this is boundary refinement of the consensus category, not equivalence, contradiction, or novelty.
strongest_objection: Consensus treats concealment as only one facet or consequence of the dominant evil/separation meaning, so equating darkness solely with ‘concealed disobedience’ under-weights the broader settled dualism.
